title.value: Search flights with an AI agent, stopping before booking

introduction.value: A travel writer had an AI agent search for flights; it took 21 minutes to find a $767 JetBlue fare, filled traveler details, and asked before booking. It was slower than manual.

method.value: Craig Stoltz asked Google's Gemini agent, which comes with a $20-a-month Google Pro subscription, to find a nonstop flight from any Washington, D.C.-area airport to Cancún, with set dates and bag rules. The agent clicked through Google Flights screens on its own. At the traveler information page it stopped, filled the fields from details Stoltz typed into the chat, and asked whether to proceed before buying.

outcome.value: It took 21 minutes to surface a $767 JetBlue fare, which Stoltz found slower and harder than booking manually. Google's AI Mode found a fare $138 cheaper in under 10 seconds, and Meta's Muse found it in three minutes.

notes.value: The agent had to stop for human input anyway, so it could not run fully in the background. Fares can also expire while a slow agent works.

source_text.body:
Search flights with an AI agent, stopping before booking
A travel writer had an AI agent search for flights; it took 21 minutes to find a $767 JetBlue fare, filled traveler details, and asked before booking. It was slower than manual.
Done with
GE
Gemini
What they did
Craig Stoltz asked Google's Gemini agent, which comes with a $20-a-month Google Pro subscription, to find a nonstop flight from any Washington, D.C.-area airport to Cancún, with set dates and bag rules. The agent clicked through Google Flights screens on its own. At the traveler information page it stopped, filled the fields from details Stoltz typed into the chat, and asked whether to proceed before buying.
How it went
It took 21 minutes to surface a $767 JetBlue fare, which Stoltz found slower and harder than booking manually. Google's AI Mode found a fare $138 cheaper in under 10 seconds, and Meta's Muse found it in three minutes.
Worth knowing
The agent had to stop for human input anyway, so it could not run fully in the background. Fares can also expire while a slow agent works.
Try it yourself
with
Operator
Copy prompt
Search for round-trip flights from [origin] to [destination], leaving [date] and returning [date], for [number] traveler(s). Compare options on [airline sites or Google Flights] and give me the best three by price and travel time, then fill in traveler details for the one I choose: [name as on ID, contact info]. Stop before payment or booking and show me the itinerary and total price to approve.
Original source: https://www.afar.com/magazine/what-uniteds-ai-booking-ban-means-for-finding-lower-fares
